questions.text: What does the lesson identify as the distinctive contribution AI makes to accessibility in the classroom?

options.text: It removes the need for teaching assistants, specialised aids and professional support staff.
It adapts content at the moment a barrier appears, without requiring specialised equipment or advance preparation.
It makes the advance preparation of adapted materials unnecessary.
It guarantees that adapted materials are accurate, so the teacher does not need to review them.

questions.explanation: The lesson describes AI as a bridge between the moment a barrier appears and the moment professional help arrives. Its distinctive value is real-time adaptation, which complements rather than replaces existing support and advance planning.

questions.text: Which of the following does the lesson place beyond the reach of AI in an accessibility context?

options.text: Producing a simplified version of a complex text in seconds
Judging whether a particular level of adaptation is pedagogically appropriate
Providing the emotional support and human connection a student needs
Transcribing a teacher's spoken explanation into text

questions.explanation: Simplifying text and transcribing speech are named among AI's practical capabilities, while assessing needs, judging pedagogical appropriateness and offering human support are listed as things AI cannot do.

questions.text: Using AI for accessibility requires teachers to first master specialised assistive technology platforms.
questions.explanation: The lesson states that most of the tools it describes run on the same general-purpose AI platforms teachers may already use for other purposes. What differs is how they are prompted and what they are asked to do.

questions.text: The lesson describes three functions the teacher performs in AI-supported accessibility. Which one is the role of the quality controller?

options.text: Reviewing AI-adapted content before it reaches the student, or teaching the student to review it critically.
Deciding at which moments AI assistance is appropriate and at which it is not.
Integrating AI accessibility tools into the wider pedagogical framework and the standard curriculum.
Recording which students in the school make the most use of AI adaptations.

questions.explanation: Deciding when AI is appropriate is the gatekeeper function and integrating the tools into the curriculum is the learning designer function. The quality controller checks the output, because a simplification that loses essential meaning is a distortion rather than an adaptation.
